trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 (Study AACI)
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline on the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) (Overall Population)
trials.results_summary: Donanemab significantly slowed clinical and cognitive decline at 76 weeks compared to placebo, showing a 22.3% reduction in decline on the iADRS and a 29% reduction in CDR-SB. ARIA was a common, known adverse event.

trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ
trials.population: Participants With Early Symptomatic Alzheimer's Disease
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) Score
trials.results_summary: Demonstrated that donanemab resulted in a better composite score for cognition and the ability to perform activities of daily living than placebo at 76 weeks.

trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 4
trials.population: Participants With Early Symptomatic Alzheimer's Disease
trials.primary_endpoint: Percentage of Participants Who Reach Complete Amyloid Plaque Clearance on Florbetapir F18 Positron Emission Tomography (PET) Scan
trials.results_summary: Demonstrated superior amyloid plaque clearance for donanemab compared to aducanumab in early, symptomatic Alzheimer's disease.

trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3
trials.primary_endpoint: Time to Clinical Progression of Composite Endpoint

related_evidence.description: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 Phase 3 trial pivotal results published in JAMA.
TRAILBLAZER-ALZ Phase 2 trial results published in NEJM.
FDA approval of Kisunla (donanemab-azbt) for early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence robustly supports the document's efficacy claims, primarily driven by the Phase 3 TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 (NCT04437511) trial, which successfully replicated the positive outcomes of the Phase 2 TRAILBLAZER-ALZ (NCT03367403) study. Donanemab demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful slowing of cognitive decline on the iADRS and CDR-SB scales compared to placebo. The safety profile, characterized by significant risks of ARIA-E and ARIA-H (particularly in ApoE ε4 carriers), is thoroughly characterized in the clinical record and aligns with class effects of anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies. Given established physician familiarity with managing ARIA risks from prior therapies (like lecanemab and aducanumab), the FDA’s decision to mandate rigorous labeling and pharmacovigilance rather than a formal REMS program is entirely consistent with the verifiable evidence and recent regulatory precedent.
discrepancies: The document reports an 'n' of 2802, while the clinical registry for the pivotal Phase 3 trial (NCT04437511) lists an enrollment of 1736; the larger number in the FDA review represents an expanded safety pool analyzing patients across multiple donanemab trials, rather than solely the primary efficacy cohort of Study AACI.
